title: Stream-aware workspace autotuner - field notes
content:
Summary:

These are field notes from an exploratory pass on a lightweight per-stream/per-model workspace autotuner. Goal was to reduce observed OOM cascades on mixed workloads where slow (long-seq) requests temporarily inflate workspace needs and cause unrelated small requests to fail. This doc captures hypotheses, experiment plans, logs, microbenchmarks, and a simple heuristic that looks promising.

Context and motivation:
- Production pool: mixed tenants, small-chat (seq<=128) + long-batch (seq>1k) inference.
- Problem: sporadic OOMs during long-tail traffic bursts. OOMs often manifest as cudaMalloc retries in driver logs followed by request timeouts and eviction churn.
- Existing mitigations (global reservation, strict per-request caps) either waste headroom or break latency SLOs for latency-sensitive requests.
- Idea: make workspace sizing aware of the GPU stream (CUDA stream used by request execution) and recent per-stream allocations; allow transient oversubscription within controlled backpressure windows to avoid retry storms.

Hypotheses:
1) OOMs are amplified by synchronous allocation retries across multiple streams when a single long request holds a large contiguous workspace for extended time (kernel stalls, host pinned page faults).
2) Moving short-lived small allocations to a per-stream bump allocator (fast freelist) reduces fragmentation and contention versus global arenas.
3) Allowing a bounded per-stream transient budget (burst credit) prevents allocation retries for small requests while a long request is draining KV cache / doing long kernels.

Experiment design:
- Branch: stream-alloc-heuristics/exp-autotune (see linked PR).
- Two runtime modes tested:
  A) baseline: global GPU mem pool + cudamallocasync arena, eviction based on global soft limit.
  B) autotune: per-stream micro-arena (64MB default), fallback to global arena on miss. Per-stream budgets tracked and decayed with configurable half-life (default 2s).
- Controlled workload on 8-GPU node: mix of 80% short requests (batch=1, seq=64, 80 qps) + 20% long requests (batch=4, seq=1536, 5 qps) for 30 minutes.
- Metrics collected: allocation latency (ms), cudaMallocAsync retry counts, peak reserved bytes per GPU, %requests that hit fallback path, p50/p95/p99 latency per class, OOM count, fragmentation estimate (reserved - allocated).

Quick repro commands (local harness):
- launcher: ./bench --model llama-7b-fp16 --streams 32 --short qps:80,bs:1,seq:64 --long qps:5,bs:4,seq:1536 --duration 1800
- runtime flags tested: --per-stream-arena=64MB --burst-credit=30MB --credit-half-life=2s --enable-stream-stats

Observed signals (raw snippets):
- baseline run (selected lines from driver logs):
  [2024-10-07 14:12:43] cudaMallocAsync failed: retrying after 3ms (attempt 1)
  [2024-10-07 14:12:43] cudaMallocAsync failed: retrying after 5ms (attempt 2)
  [2024-10-07 14:12:43] kernel launch blocked on mem, stream 0x7f9b3c, holding 185MB workspace
  [2024-10-07 14:12:44] eviction: reclaimed 210MB KV entries across 3 contexts
  [2024-10-07 14:12:44] request_fail: id=....15ms alloc-fail
- autotune run (selected lines):
  [2024-10-07 16:02:10] per-stream 0x7f9b3c alloc 8MB -> within micro-arena
  [2024-10-07 16:02:10] per-stream credit used 28MB/30MB
  [2024-10-07 16:02:10] short request served, latency 14ms (p50)
  [2024-10-07 16:02:10] long request holding 190MB global arena (expected)
  [2024-10-07 16:02:11] fallback->global arena (per-stream exhausted)
  [2024-10-07 16:02:11] 0 cudaMalloc retries observed in 1m window

Results summary (30m runs):
- Baseline:
  - OOMs: 6 total (clustered during two long-request peaks)
  - cudaMalloc retry spikes: 120 events/min at peak
  - p99 short-request latency: 320ms (timeout spikes)
  - fragmentation estimate (end of run): reserved 22.3GB, committed 18.1GB -> wasted ~4.2GB (~19%)
- Autotune (per-stream micro-arenas + burst credit):
  - OOMs: 0 in same run conditions
  - cudaMalloc retry spikes: eliminated (<=3 events/min)
  - p99 short-request latency: 62ms
  - fragmentation estimate: reserved 21.6GB, committed 19.8GB -> wasted ~1.8GB (~8%)
  - %requests that needed global fallback: 6.3% (mostly long requests or rare concurrent bursts)

Interpretation and notes:
- Per-stream micro-arenas reduced allocation latency for short requests significantly. This cut down the retry cascade effect because small requests no longer hit the global arena while a long request holds a large contiguous region.
- Burst credits (30MB by default) acted as a shock absorber for transient spikes. Tuning credit size is workload-dependent; too large defeats reservation goals, too small reintroduces retries.
- Fragmentation dropped vs baseline because micro-arenas favor reuse on the same stream and reduce cross-stream free-list churn.
- We observed a secondary effect: pinned host allocations during some long requests caused kernel stalls that made workspace appear 'held' longer than kernel runtime. This was visible in host-side page-fault logs and increased per-stream credit consumption.

Telemetry caveats / what to watch for in production:
- Ensure credit half-life decay is tuned for traffic burstiness. Very bursty traffic benefits from faster decay to free credits quickly.
- Track stream-id churn: ephemeral streams (created per-request) reduce effectiveness of per-stream arenas; better when runtime reuses streams per worker thread.
- Watch for multi-tenant fairness: long-running tenants could exhaust all per-stream budgets if they pin streams; add tenant-level throttles or max-credit-per-tenant.
- Interaction with OS-level hugepage allocations/pinning: some hosts showed large host-pinned allocations during warmup; this increases risk of GPU-visible stall.

Implementation notes / snippets:
- micro-arena: simple bump-pointer with small freelist for common sizes (64B, 256B, 4KB, 1MB). Fast path uses atomic offset on per-stream struct.
- credit accounting: atomic per-stream counter (bytes); on allocation attempt: if size <= micro-arena_free and credit_available apply; else try global arena. On free: decrease credit_counter. Decay: scheduled timer every 250ms applies half-life factor.
- fallback metrics: increment histogram for alerting when fallback_rate > 5% over 5min window.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should per-stream arenas be per-worker instead? That would make streams irrelevant to effectiveness but may increase tail contention between threads. Need microbench.
- Would a fast shared small-size slab (per-GPU) + per-stream credit for mid-size allocations be simpler and equally effective?
- Need a deterministic repro that reproduces the pinned-host page-fault induced stalls — suspected race between network DMA, pinned pages, and host-to-device copies.
- Add a safety path: if global arena fragmentation passes X% and fallback_rate high, temporarily shrink burst-credit to 0 and prioritize eviction.

Next steps:
- Run 24h soak with 4-node cluster and more realistic tenant mix (3 tenants with independent traffic shapes). Capture debug traces for any OOMs. (Assigned: Arjun)
- Prototype per-worker arena variant and compare to per-stream (Lena).
- Add tenant-level credit caps and test for fairness regressions (Omar).
- Post a short note to SRE and Product about possible operational knob: --burst-credit-size and --enable-per-stream-arenas (include perf numbers).

Appendix: microbench numbers (local)
- alloc latency microbench (ns):
  baseline global-calls median 4500ns, p99 24000ns
  micro-arena median 320ns, p99 1500ns
- sample flamegraph note: hotspots shift from allocator slow-path (~25% cpu) to small bookkeeping (~8%) when micro-arenas enabled.

Quick logs to keep: attached in PR (see linked_artifacts) — includes allocation traces, per-stream credit timeline CSV, and flamegraphs.

Notes to self:
- good to keep default burst-credit small (16-64MB) and configurable by customer tier; enterprise can allocate higher.
- watch for complexity creep: prefer heuristic simple enough to explain to on-call.

End of notes.
